paragraphs.heading: Two crystals sharing a pattern
paragraphs.text: Crystal twinning happens when two or more adjacent crystals of one mineral are lined up so that some of their crystal lattice points are shared in a symmetrical way. The outcome is an intergrowth: two separate crystals tightly bonded to each other. The surface where the shared points lie is called a composition surface or twin plane.

paragraphs.heading: Not a random join
paragraphs.text: Twinning is not the same as the ordinary, random way mineral grains grow together in a mineral deposit. In a twin, the two crystal segments are oriented relative to each other in a fixed way that is characteristic of the mineral structure. A symmetry operation, called a twin operation, defines that fixed relationship. A twin operation is not among the normal symmetry operations that the untwinned crystal structure has. It may be a reflection, for example, across a plane that the single crystal does not have as a symmetry plane.

paragraphs.heading: Why twins hold together
paragraphs.text: At the microscopic level, a twin boundary is marked by a group of atomic positions in the lattice that the two orientations share. These shared lattice points make the junction between the crystal segments much stronger than the junction between randomly oriented grains. As a result, twinned crystals do not easily break apart.

paragraphs.heading: Three main types
paragraphs.text: There are three main types of twinning. Growth twinning can occur in very large particles and in very small ones. In transformation twinning there is a change in the crystal structure. Deformation twinning arises when a shear stress acts on a crystal, and it is an important mechanism for permanent changes in the crystal's shape.

paragraphs.heading: Twin laws
paragraphs.text: Twinned crystals are described by twin laws, which are symmetry operations that define the orientation between the twin crystal segments. Twin laws are specific to the crystal structure, and they are as characteristic of a mineral as its crystal face angles are. Crystals of staurolite, for example, twin at angles of almost exactly 90 degrees or 30 degrees. Twin laws can be reflection operations, rotation operations or the inversion operation. The type of twinning can be used as a diagnostic tool in identifying a mineral.

paragraphs.heading: Contact twins
paragraphs.text: Simple twinned crystals come in two kinds, contact twins and penetration twins. Contact twins meet on a single composition plane and often look like mirror images across the boundary. Plagioclase, quartz, gypsum and spinel often show contact twinning. A characteristic sign is the reentrant face, where faces of the crystal segments come together at the contact plane, making an angle of more than 180°.

paragraphs.heading: A lookalike that is not a twin
paragraphs.text: Parallel growth is a form of crystal growth that produces what looks like a cluster of aligned crystals, and the cluster could be mistaken for twins. Close examination shows that it is actually a single crystal. Because the crystal lattice is continuous through the whole cluster, this does not count as twinning.
